cemc-hypatia-2020-01a.title: Subtract the avocados
cemc-hypatia-2020-01a.body:
12 bags of avocados cost $12 \times 5 = 60$ dollars, leaving $135 - 60 = 75$ dollars for mangoes: $75 \div 12.50 = 6$ boxes.

**Answer: 6 boxes**

cemc-hypatia-2020-01b.title: Discounted prices
cemc-hypatia-2020-01b.body:
A bag costs $0.9 \times 5 = 4.50$ dollars and a box costs $0.8 \times 12.50 = 10.00$ dollars. Total: $8(4.50) + 4(10.00) = 36 + 40 = 76$ dollars.

**Answer: \$76.00**

cemc-hypatia-2020-01b.title: Discount on the totals
cemc-hypatia-2020-01b.body:
At regular prices: $8 \times 5 = 40$ and $4 \times 12.50 = 50$. Discounts: $10\%$ of 40 is 4, $20\%$ of 50 is 10. Total $= 90 - 14 = 76$ dollars.

**Answer: \$76.00**

cemc-hypatia-2020-01c.title: Round up
cemc-hypatia-2020-01c.body:
$6 \times 16 = 96 < 100 \le 102 = 6 \times 17$, so she needs 17 bags. $15 \times 4 = 60 < 70 \le 75 = 15 \times 5$, so she needs 5 boxes. Cost: $17 \times 5 + 5 \times 12.50 = 85 + 62.50 = 147.50$ dollars.

**Answer: \$147.50**

cemc-hypatia-2020-01d.title: Even number of boxes
cemc-hypatia-2020-01d.body:
Avocado costs are whole dollars, and $m$ boxes of mangoes cost $12.5m$, a whole number only for even $m$. Since $\$75$ is whole, $m \in \{0, 2, 4, 6\}$:

| boxes | bags ($= (75 - 12.5m)/5$) | mangoes | avocados | tarts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 15 | 0 | 90 | 0 |
| 2 | 10 | 30 | 60 | 15 |
| 4 | 5 | 60 | 30 | 30 |
| 6 | 0 | 90 | 0 | 0 |

The number of tarts is $\min(\text{avocados}, \text{mangoes}/2)$. The maximum is **30**.

**Answer: 30**

cemc-hypatia-2020-02a.title: Symmetry
cemc-hypatia-2020-02a.body:
By symmetry in the $y$-axis the other vertex on the parabola is $(-6, 9)$ (check: $\frac14 \cdot 36 = 9$). The two vertices on the $x$-axis lie directly below: $(6, 0)$ and $(-6, 0)$.

**Answer: $(-6, 9)$, $(6, 0)$, $(-6, 0)$**

cemc-hypatia-2020-02b.title: Length times height
cemc-hypatia-2020-02b.body:
The other bottom vertex is $(3, 0)$, so the length is 6. The top vertices are on the parabola above $x = \pm 3$, at height $\frac14 \cdot 9 = \frac94$. Area $= 6 \cdot \frac94 = \frac{27}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{27}{2}$**

cemc-hypatia-2020-02b.title: General formula
cemc-hypatia-2020-02b.body:
A parabolic rectangle with bottom vertices $(\pm p, 0)$ has area $2p \cdot \frac{p^2}{4} = \frac{p^3}{2}$. With $p = 3$: $\frac{27}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{27}{2}$**

cemc-hypatia-2020-02c.title: Length or width equals 36
cemc-hypatia-2020-02c.body:
With bottom vertices $(\pm p, 0)$, $p > 0$, the rectangle has length $2p$, width $\frac14 p^2$ and area $\frac12 p^3$.

- Length 36: $p = 18$, area $\frac12 \cdot 18^3 = 2916$.
- Width 36: $p^2 = 144$, $p = 12$, area $\frac12 \cdot 12^3 = 864$.

**Answer: 2916 and 864**

cemc-hypatia-2020-02d.title: Solve 2m = m²/4
cemc-hypatia-2020-02d.body:
With bottom vertices $(\pm m, 0)$: length $2m$, width $\frac14 m^2$. Equal when $\frac14 m^2 = 2m$, i.e. $m(m - 8) = 0$, so $m = 8$. Then the rectangle is a $16 \times 16$ square with area $256$.

**Answer: 256**

cemc-hypatia-2020-02d.title: Square on the parabola
cemc-hypatia-2020-02d.body:
A square of side $s$ has top corners $(\pm \frac s2, s)$ on the parabola: $s = \frac14 \cdot \frac{s^2}{4}$, so $s = 16$ and the area is $256$.

**Answer: 256**

cemc-hypatia-2020-03a.title: Draw one triangulation
cemc-hypatia-2020-03a.body:
Put one point $P$ inside the triangle and join it to the 3 vertices: 3 triangles. Put the second point $Q$ inside one of these and join it to that triangle's 3 vertices: that triangle becomes 3, so the total is $3 - 1 + 3 = 5$.

**Answer: 5**

cemc-hypatia-2020-03a.title: Angle sum
cemc-hypatia-2020-03a.body:
Count angles: the triangles' angles add up to the triangle's $180°$ plus $360°$ around each interior point: $180° + 2 \cdot 360° = 900° = 5 \cdot 180°$. So there are 5 triangles.

**Answer: 5**

cemc-hypatia-2020-03b.title: Each interior point adds 2 triangles
cemc-hypatia-2020-03b.body:
$T(4, 0) = 2$ (a diagonal splits the square into 2 triangles). Since $T$ does not depend on the triangulation, build one point by point: a new interior point lies inside some triangle of the current triangulation (it can't be on an edge, as no three points are collinear); joining it to that triangle's 3 vertices replaces 1 triangle by 3, a net gain of 2. So $T(4, k) = 2 + 2k$ and $T(4, 100) = 202$.

**Answer: 202**

cemc-hypatia-2020-03b.title: Angle sum
cemc-hypatia-2020-03b.body:
The angles of all triangles add up to the square's interior angles $360°$ plus $360°$ around each interior point: $360° (1 + 100) = 36\,360°$. Dividing by $180°$ gives $202$ triangles.

**Answer: 202**

cemc-hypatia-2020-03c.title: General formula
cemc-hypatia-2020-03c.body:
With no interior points, joining one vertex to the $n - 3$ non-adjacent vertices gives $T(n, 0) = n - 2$. As in (b), each interior point adds 2 triangles, so $T(n, k) = n - 2 + 2k$. Then $T(n, n) = 3n - 2 = 2020$ gives $n = 674$.

**Answer: 674**

cemc-hypatia-2020-03c.title: Angle sum
cemc-hypatia-2020-03c.body:
The triangles' angles total $(n - 2) \cdot 180°$ (the polygon) plus $k \cdot 360°$, so $T(n, k) = n - 2 + 2k$. Setting $k = n$: $3n - 2 = 2020$, $n = 674$.

**Answer: 674**

cemc-hypatia-2020-04a.title: Parity flips each step
cemc-hypatia-2020-04a.body: $x^2$ has the same parity as $x$, so $x_{i+1} = x_i^2 + 1$ has the opposite parity to $x_i$. Applying this twice, $x_2$ has the same parity as $x_0$, so $x_2 - x_0$ is even. ∎

cemc-hypatia-2020-04a.title: Algebra
cemc-hypatia-2020-04a.body:
$x_2 = (x_0^2 + 1)^2 + 1 = x_0^4 + 2x_0^2 + 2$, so

$$x_2 - x_0 = x_0^2(x_0^2 + 1) + x_0(x_0 - 1) + 2.$$

Each of $x_0^2(x_0^2 + 1)$ and $x_0(x_0 - 1)$ is a product of two consecutive integers, hence even, so $x_2 - x_0$ is even. ∎

cemc-hypatia-2020-04b.title: Units-digit table
cemc-hypatia-2020-04b.body:
The units digit of $x_{i+1}$ is the units digit of $u^2 + 1$, where $u$ is the units digit of $x_i$. So the map on units digits is

$$0 \to 1,\ 1 \to 2,\ 2 \to 5,\ 3 \to 0,\ 4 \to 7,\ 5 \to 6,\ 6 \to 7,\ 7 \to 0,\ 8 \to 5,\ 9 \to 2.$$

Following it, $1 \to 2 \to 5 \to 6 \to 7 \to 0 \to 1$ is a cycle of length 6, and every digit is either on it ($0,1,2,5,6,7$) or maps into it in one step ($3 \to 0$, $4 \to 7$, $8 \to 5$, $9 \to 2$). Hence $x_1, x_2, \ldots$ all have units digits on the 6-cycle, and $x_{i+6}$ has the same units digit as $x_i$ for all $i \ge 1$.

Since $2026 = 2020 + 6$, $x_{2026}$ and $x_{2020}$ have the same units digit, so their difference is divisible by 10. ∎

cemc-hypatia-2020-04c.title: Work modulo 3, 5 and 7
cemc-hypatia-2020-04c.body:
$x_{115} - 110 \equiv x_{115} - 5 \pmod{105}$, and $105 = 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$, so we need $x_{115} \equiv 5$ modulo each of 3, 5, 7.

**Mod 3.** The map $r \mapsto r^2 + 1$ sends $0 \to 1 \to 2 \to 2$. So $x_i \equiv 2 \equiv 5 \pmod 3$ for all $i \ge 2$: always satisfied.

**Mod 5.** Need $x_{115} \equiv 0$. The map is $0 \to 1 \to 2 \to 0$ and $3 \to 0$, $4 \to 2$, so from $x_1$ on the residues cycle with period 3. As $115 \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, $x_{115} \equiv x_4 \equiv x_1 \pmod 5$, and $x_1 \equiv 0$ exactly when $x_0 \equiv 2$ or $3 \pmod 5$. (Check: $x_0 \equiv 2$: $x_1 \equiv 0$.)

**Mod 7.** The map is $0 \to 1 \to 2 \to 5 \to 5$, $6 \to 2$, $3 \to 3$, $4 \to 3$. So $x_{115} \equiv 5 \pmod 7$ unless $x_0 \equiv 3$ or $4 \pmod 7$ (then it stays at 3 forever).

**Count.** We need $x_0 \equiv 2, 3 \pmod 5$ and $x_0 \not\equiv 3, 4 \pmod 7$. Modulo 35 that is $2 \times 5 = 10$ residues: $2, 7, 8, 12, 13, 22, 23, 27, 28, 33$. In $1..100$: 10 in $1..35$, 10 in $36..70$, and in $71..100$ the values $72, 77, 78, 82, 83, 92, 93, 97, 98$ (9 of them, since $103 > 100$). Total 29.

Probability $= \frac{29}{100}$.

**Answer: $\frac{29}{100}$**
